memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me warn you of what this people will do to your people in days to come." Then he spoke his message: "The prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of one whose eye sees clearly, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate, and whose eyes are opened." - Num 24:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before he departs, Balaam speaks one final oracle, looking far ahead to "days to come." Once more he describes himself as one whose eyes are opened, who hears the words of God and has knowledge from the Most High. What follows will be his most far-reaching vision, a glimpse into the distant future.

There is a solemn weight to these words. Balaam is about to speak of things that will unfold long after his own lifetime, matters known only to God. The Most High was granting him a vision of what He had purposed. Only God knows the future, and only God can reveal it.

We are reminded that history is not a series of random events but the unfolding of God's sovereign plan. From the plains of Moab, the Lord was already looking ahead to what He would do in generations to come. Nothing about the future is uncertain to Him. He sees the end from the beginning.

This gives us confidence as we face our own unknown tomorrows. The God who revealed the distant future to Balaam holds our future securely in His hands. In Christ, we know that the One who began a good work will carry it to completion (Phil 1:6). We may not see what lies ahead, but we trust the God who does.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust God with a future you cannot see?
2. How does God's knowledge of all things comfort you in uncertainty?
3. What does it mean to rest in God's sovereign plan for history?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, You alone see the end from the beginning. When my future feels uncertain, help me to trust the One who holds all things and completes the work He begins in Christ. Amen.
